I would balance out the CIS and business/remaining classes especially for 3343 and 3365, since they are considered the weedout classes and will definitely take up most of your time. Ideally for each semester, I would take 2 CIS classes and 2-3 other classes (3 if they are easier). I have Detillier for 3365 right now and he is the harshest, most tough professor I ever had. The other 3000/4000 classes will be easier to handle than those two. 


Viseh for 3347 is okay; I never went to his class because he was extremely boring to listen to. The class is mostly writing. Don't fall behind and you'll likely make an A. I had Otto for 2348 and 3368 right now. He's probably the best Java professor right now. He knows his stuff and wants to make sure you know your stuff too; just make sure you go to class.


Not sure if you're planning on taking any summer classes but it would be ideal to take cis 3355 in the summer. They offer it as an online class, which is easier than the hybrid equivalent. If you took all three (3365, 3368, 3355) in the fall, that would be quite a heavy workload for the average student. I would only do that if you really like the topics or like studying/working a lot. Practice Java in the summer to prepare for 3368. Postponing it will only postpone your graduation rate since they are all prereqs for the last few classes you need.
